one_liner: Senior supervisor at the White House Communications Agency (DISA) overseeing program analysis, acquisition, budget and personnel/admin functions through subordinate supervisors.
fit_summary: This GG-14 supervisory role needs a year of experience equivalent to GS/GG-13 in program evaluation, acquisition, budget execution, or administrative management, plus SCI clearance eligibility. Daniel's IEM consulting background may touch program analysis for government clients, but nothing on file shows senior-level budget, acquisition, or supervisory experience. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills are not what this posting screens for.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no federal status required, but it is Cyber Excepted Service and does not convert to competitive service.

Specialized experience: one year at the GG/GS-13 equivalent evaluating complex programs and resource requirements, coordinating acquisition actions, overseeing budget execution, resolving funding issues, or managing administrative processes.
No education substitution at GG-14; experience must be shown in the resume body.
Must obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI clearance (White House Communications Agency), which likely means an extensive background investigation.
All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the November 2, 2026 closing date.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work included at least a year of senior-level program evaluation, budget/funding tracking, or acquisition/contract support. If not, target GS-9 to GS-12 program analyst or emergency management roles (e.g., FEMA, Virginia VDEM, Prince William County OEM) instead.

If you apply, frame IEM work around government client programs: evaluating disaster recovery or preparedness programs, tracking grant or project funding, supporting task orders or contract deliverables, and leading teams. Use the posting's exact phrases.
Preview the questionnaire at the link in the posting and answer each item at the level your resume can prove. The agency explicitly checks for inflated answers.
Keep to two pages: for each job list dates, hours per week, and two or three specialized-experience bullets mapped to the qualifying experience statement.
Apply well before November 2, 2026; the window is only about 12 days after the October 21 opening.
resume_bullets: Evaluated [number] [type of disaster recovery/preparedness] programs for [government client], identifying [resource gaps/operational risks] and recommending [specific improvements] adopted by [client].
Tracked budget execution of $[amount] in [grant/project/task order] funds for [client], resolving [type of funding issue] in coordination with [contracting/finance staff].
Led a team of [number] [staff/contractor] personnel, assigning work, setting priorities, and monitoring milestones to deliver [deliverable] by [deadline].
interview_questions: Describe a time you analyzed a complex program and found systemic issues or resource gaps. What did you recommend, and what happened?
How have you developed an acquisition strategy or conducted market research, and how did you work with contracting officers?
Tell us about resolving a funding shortfall or budget execution problem under deadline pressure.
How would you supervise a mixed civilian, military, and contractor workforce through subordinate supervisors, including handling performance issues?
watch_outs: Grade and supervisory level likely far exceed your documented experience; an over-reaching application risks a 'not qualified' rating.
Requires a TS/SCI clearance and White House support work, with a lengthy investigation.
Cyber Excepted Service does not give competitive-service status, which limits later transfer to other federal jobs.
